claims.title: Hafit-period tombs near Jebel Hafit
claims.summary: Beehive-shaped stone tombs of the Hafit period appear on the slopes of Jebel Hafit near Al Ain, the earliest monumental architecture of the region and a marker of settled life at the desert's edge.

sources.label: Cultural Sites of Al Ain (Hafit, Hili, Bidaa Bint Saud and Oases Areas)

claims.title: The Umm an-Nar culture flourishes
claims.summary: Named for an island off Abu Dhabi, the Umm an-Nar culture built circular communal tombs, fortified towers and agricultural settlements at Hili, trading copper and goods with Mesopotamia and the Indus valley.

claims.title: The aflaj irrigation system at Hili
claims.summary: Hili preserves one of the oldest known examples of the aflaj, underground channels that carried mountain groundwater to oasis date gardens, sustaining agriculture in an arid land.

claims.summary: The Trucial rulers agreed to cede no territory and form no foreign relations except through Britain, in return for British protection, making the coast in effect a British protected zone.
